\section{Introduction}
\begin{theorem}[Main theorem]\label{thm:intro}
For every $n > 2$ there are no positive integers $a,b,c$ with $a^n + b^n = c^n$.
\end{theorem}

\section{Main results}
\begin{definition}\label{def:nice}
A group is nice if it is abelian.
\end{definition}
\begin{theorem}\label{thm:main}
Every finite group $G$ of odd order is solvable.
\end{theorem}
\begin{corollary}\label{cor:simple}
Every finite simple group of odd order is cyclic of prime order.
\end{corollary}
\begin{lemma}
If $p$ is prime then $p \mid \binom{p}{k}$ for $0<k<p$.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proposition}\label{prop:sorry}
The sum of two even numbers is even.
\end{proposition}
